# Spec format

<!-- Generated by `uv run python -m ditto.specgen.schema_export` from src/ditto/specgen/models.py and the lint, transform, runner and typecheck modules. Do not edit by hand. -->

A spec is one versioned JSON file per template. It holds XPath 1.0 selectors plus a closed set of
transforms, never code. Validation compiles every selector and lints it (see `lint.py`),
parses every transform (see `transforms.py`) and checks indices and names; a spec that loads
is a spec that runs.

The JSON Schema is [`spec.schema.json`](spec.schema.json). In Python, `Spec.load(path)` validates a spec file and `spec.apply(html)` runs it on one page with no other machinery.

## Field types

| `type` | Output | Shape |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `scalar` | string, number or null | One value or null. The selector must match exactly one node where the field exists; extraction keeps the first non-null match. |
| `list` | array | An array of values: every node the selector matches (0..N), in document order. |
| `record_list` | array of objects | An array of objects: `container` matches each row, each column XPath is relative to the row. Rows whose columns are all null are dropped. |
| `key_value` | object | An object: `pairs` matches one element per pair, `key` and `value` are relative to it. Keys lose a trailing colon; the first occurrence of a key wins. |

## Top-level keys

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `spec_version` | `"1"` | `"1"` | Format version; `"1"` for this release. |
| `template_id` | string, non-empty | **required** | Template (cluster) id, e.g. `t_3f9a`. |
| `site` | string, non-empty | **required** | Site the template belongs to (its domain). |
| `status` | `"draft"` or `"final"` | `"draft"` | `draft` after generation, `final` once verification selected candidates. |
| `generated_by` | object (`GeneratedBy`) | **required** | Provenance (see `generated_by`). |
| `fields` | object: name → one of object (`ScalarField`), object (`ListField`), object (`RecordListField`), object (`KeyValueField`) | **required** | Output field name -> field definition. Names are the keys of every extracted record; `url`, `page_id`, `template_id` and names starting with `_` are reserved. |
| `not_present` | object: name → string | `{}` | Prompted fields the LLM could not find -> reason. |

### `generated_by`

Provenance: which model and prompt wrote the spec, from which pages. Extra keys allowed.

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `model` | string | **required** | Model id that wrote the spec. |
| `prompt_version` | string | **required** | Prompt id used for generation, e.g. `specgen.v1`. |
| `pages_seen` | array of string | `[]` | URLs of the pages merged into the union page. |
| `mode` | `"prompted"` or `"unprompted"` or `"fallback"` | `"prompted"` | `prompted` (user fields.yaml), `unprompted` (LLM named the fields) or `fallback` (path-induced selectors, no LLM). |
| `repair_calls` | integer ≥ 0 | `0` | Repair LLM calls spent on this spec. |
| `repair_prompt_version` | string or null | `null` | Prompt id used for repair, e.g. `repair.v1`. |
| `created_at` | string or null | `null` | ISO 8601 creation time. |

## Field definitions

Keys every field type accepts:

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `description` | string or null | `null` | What the field holds, in words (from fields.yaml or the LLM). |
| `optional` | boolean | `false` | True when the analysis found the field's path on fewer than 95% of the cluster's pages, so a null is not a failure. |
| `degraded` | boolean | `false` | Set by verification when the field still fails on some pages after the repair budget is spent; see `stats` for its rates. |
| `selection_reason` | string or null | `null` | Why verification picked the selected candidate. |
| `source_candidates` | array of string | `[]` | Analysis candidate ids (e.g. c17) this field maps to. |
| `stats` | object (`FieldStats`) | `{}` | Verification statistics (see `stats`). |

### `scalar` and `list`

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `type` | `"scalar"` | `"scalar"` | Field type discriminator. |
| `candidates` | array of string (2–3 items) | **required** | Two or three distinct absolute XPath 1.0 selectors for the same value. |
| `selected` | integer ≥ 0 | `0` | Index of the candidate extraction uses (set by verification). |
| `fallbacks` | array of integer | `[]` | Candidate indices tried in order when the selected one matches nothing; verification only lists candidates that agree with the winner. |
| `transforms` | array of string | `[]` | Transforms applied in order to each matched item (closed set: strip, normalize_ws, regex(pattern, group), split(sep, index), replace(old, new), cast(int\|float\|date), attr(name)). |
| `type_check` | `"email"` or `"url"` or `"number"` or `"date"` or `"price"` or `"text"` or null | `null` | Expected value type, checked by verification. |

`type` is `"list"` for a list field; the other keys are identical.

### `record_list`

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `type` | `"record_list"` | `"record_list"` | Field type discriminator. |
| `container` | string | **required** | Absolute XPath matching every row element. |
| `container_alternates` | array of string (at most 2) | `[]` | Up to two alternative container selectors (the 2-3 candidates rule); verification may promote one, extraction uses `container` only. |
| `columns` | object: name → string (at least 1) | **required** | Column name -> XPath relative to the row (starts with `.`). With `column_source: header_row` cells are addressed by header text, never by position. |
| `column_source` | `"header_row"` or `"llm"` | `"llm"` | `header_row` when column names came from `<th>` text, `llm` when the LLM named them (headerless tables may then address cells by position). |
| `transforms` | object: name → array of string | `{}` | Column name -> transform chain for that column. |

### `key_value`

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `type` | `"key_value"` | `"key_value"` | Field type discriminator. |
| `pairs` | string | **required** | Absolute XPath matching one element per key/value pair. |
| `pairs_alternates` | array of string (at most 2) | `[]` | Up to two alternative pair selectors (the 2-3 candidates rule); extraction uses `pairs` only. |
| `key` | string | `"."` | XPath relative to the pair element for the key. |
| `value` | string | **required** | XPath relative to the pair element for the value. |
| `transforms` | object: `key` or `value` → array of string | `{}` | Transform chains for `key` and/or `value`. |

### `stats`

Per-field statistics written by verification over every page of the cluster; kept in the spec for drift detection on later crawls. Extra keys are allowed.

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `presence_rate` | number in [0, 1] or null | `null` | Share of pages where the field has a value. |
| `expected_presence` | number in [0, 1] or null | `null` | Presence rate the analysis expected from the field's path (`p`). |
| `multiplicity` | number ≥ 0 or null | `null` | For scalars: share of pages with a match where the selector matched exactly one node. |
| `type_check_pass` | number in [0, 1] or null | `null` | Share of extracted values that pass the field's `type_check`. |
| `rows_min` | integer ≥ 0 or null | `null` | record_list: fewest rows on a page where present. |
| `rows_max` | integer ≥ 0 or null | `null` | record_list: most rows on a page where present. |
| `keys_seen` | integer ≥ 0 or null | `null` | key_value: distinct keys seen across the cluster. |
| `pages_scored` | integer ≥ 0 or null | `null` | Pages the statistics were computed on. |

## Selector rules

Rules (each violation yields one message):

* the selector compiles with `lxml.etree.XPath`;
* only the XPath 1.0 core function library: `matches()`, `lower-case()`, `upper-case()`
  and `ends-with()` are named explicitly in the error; any other function (XPath 2.0, XSLT,
  EXSLT), any namespace prefix and any `$variable` is rejected too (lxml compiles some of these
  and only fails when the selector runs);
* no `comment()` node test and no `data-x-` anywhere: both exist only in the annotated
  union page shown to the LLM, never in the pages the spec runs on;
* absolute selectors are location paths starting with `/`, optionally parenthesized as in
  `(//h1)[1]`; relative selectors (record columns, key/value parts) start with `.`; every
  branch of a `|` union obeys the same rule;
* no purely positional paths. After ignoring attribute, `text()`/`node()` and `.`/`..`
  steps, a selector whose every step is a bare tag (any axis, or `*`) with at most positional
  predicates (`[2]`, `[last()]`, `[position()=2]`) is unanchored. An unanchored absolute
  selector is rejected when it is rooted at `/`, carries a positional predicate, or ends on a
  generic tag (`div`, `span`, `td`, ...); descendant-anchored semantic tags such as
  `//header//h1` pass. An unanchored relative selector (anchored by its row) is rejected when
  it carries a positional predicate or steps through a cell or wildcard (`td`, `th`, `*`):
  columns are addressed by header text, so `./td[2]` fails while `.//a/@href` passes.
  Anchors are `@id`, classes, `data-*`, `itemprop` and other attributes, text predicates
  such as `normalize-space()='Email'`, or structural proximity to an anchored step, so
  `//dt[normalize-space()='Email']/following-sibling::dd[1]` passes. Headerless tables and
  key/value parts may be positional (`allow_positional`).

## Transforms

| Transform | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `strip` | Trim leading and trailing whitespace. |
| `normalize_ws` | Collapse every whitespace run (including NBSP) to one space and trim. |
| `regex(pattern, group)` | Search the text with the Python regular expression `pattern` and keep capture `group` (default 0, the whole match). No match gives null. |
| `split(sep, index)` | Split on the literal `sep` and keep piece `index` (negative counts from the end), trimmed. An index out of range gives null. |
| `replace(old, new)` | Replace every literal occurrence of `old` with `new`. |
| `cast(int\|float\|date)` | `int`/`float`: the first number in the text (`1,234.50`, `€1.234,56`, `1 234,5`); `int` truncates toward zero. `date`: the first date as ISO 8601 (`March 3, 2021` -> `2021-03-03`; `March 2021` -> `2021-03`). Unparseable text gives null. |
| `attr(name)` | Attribute `name` of the matched element (`href`, `src`, `content`, ...). Gives null when the value is not an element or the attribute is missing. |

Grammar (one string per transform):

```text
transform := name | name "(" args ")"
strip | normalize_ws                 no arguments
regex(<pattern>, <group>)            <group> is a non-negative int; omitted means 0
split(<sep>, <index>)                <index> is an int; negative counts from the end
replace(<old>, <new>)                <old> must not be empty
cast(int|float|date)
attr(<name>)                         attribute value of the matched element
```

Arguments are separated by commas. An argument may be quoted with `'...'` or `"..."`;
inside quotes `\'`/`\"` stands for the quote character and `\\` for one backslash, and
commas and spaces are literal. Unquoted arguments are trimmed and cannot contain commas, except
that an unquoted `regex` pattern extends to the last comma. Any other name, arity or argument
fails validation.

Values: each transform receives one XPath result item (an element, a string from `text()` or
`@attr`, or a number/boolean from an XPath expression) or the previous transform's output.
Elements are read as their whitespace-normalized text. `attr` needs an element. A step that
produces nothing (no regex match, index out of range, unparseable cast, missing attribute) makes
the whole chain produce `null`. The final value is a trimmed string, an `int`/`float` from
`cast`, or `null` when empty.

## Extraction semantics

What each field type extracts:

* `scalar`: evaluate `candidates[selected]`, apply `transforms` to each match in document
  order and keep the first non-null value. When the selected candidate yields nothing, try the
  `fallbacks` indices in order. Nothing found gives `null`.
* `list`: every non-null transformed match of the selected candidate, in document order; when
  that is empty, the first fallback that yields a non-empty list. Nothing found gives `[]`.
* `record_list`: every element matched by `container` is a row; each column XPath runs
  relative to the row and is reduced like a scalar (first non-null value after the column's
  transforms). Rows whose columns are all null are skipped. Nothing found gives `[]`.
* `key_value`: every element matched by `pairs` yields a key (`key`, default `.`) and a
  value (`value`), each relative to the pair element and reduced like a scalar with its
  transforms. Keys are whitespace-normalized with a trailing colon removed; pairs without a
  key are skipped; the first occurrence of a key wins (its value may be null). Nothing found
  gives `{}`.
* `container_alternates`/`pairs_alternates` are candidates for verification; extraction
  uses `container`/`pairs` only.

Values are strings (elements read as whitespace-normalized text, `text()`/`@attr` results
trimmed), numbers only from `cast`. Selectors are compiled once per process; a selector that
fails at evaluation time yields no matches. A field is *missing* on a page when its value is
`null`, `[]` or `{}`.

## Value types (`type_check`)

Value parsing and type checks shared by transforms (`cast`), analysis (`value_type`),
verification (`type_check_pass`) and probe.

* `parse_number` reads the first number in a string, understanding `1,234.50`,
  `1.234,56`, `1 234,56` (NBSP / narrow NBSP), `1'234.50` and Indian `1,23,456`.
  A single `.` is always a decimal mark; a single `,` is a thousands separator only when
  exactly three digits follow it (`1,234` -> 1234, `0,5` -> 0.5).
* `parse_date` finds the first date in a string and returns it in ISO 8601 form:
  `YYYY-MM-DD`; `YYYY-MM` for month-and-year values; `YYYY` when the whole value is a
  year. It understands ISO dates and datetimes, `March 3, 2021`, `3 Mar 2021`,
  `12-Mar-2021`, `3 de marzo de 2021`, `3. März 2021` (English, German, French,
  Spanish, Italian, Portuguese and Dutch month names) and numeric `d/m/y` forms (`/` is read
  month-first, `.` and `-` day-first, unless one part is above 12).
* `check_value` is strict: the *whole* value must have the type (`"Email: a@b.org"` is
  not an email).

## Example

The example from the product brief:

```json
{
  "spec_version": "1",
  "template_id": "t_3f9a",
  "site": "example.org",
  "generated_by": {
    "model": "<model id>",
    "prompt_version": "specgen.v1",
    "pages_seen": [
      "/staff/a-khoury",
      "/staff/l-haddad"
    ]
  },
  "fields": {
    "name": {
      "type": "scalar",
      "candidates": [
        "//h1[@itemprop='name']",
        "//header//h1"
      ],
      "selected": 0,
      "transforms": [
        "normalize_ws"
      ],
      "stats": {
        "presence_rate": 1.0,
        "multiplicity": 1.0,
        "type_check_pass": 1.0
      }
    },
    "email": {
      "type": "scalar",
      "candidates": [
        "//dt[normalize-space()='Email']/following-sibling::dd[1]//a",
        "//a[starts-with(@href,'mailto:')]"
      ],
      "selected": 0,
      "transforms": [
        "normalize_ws"
      ],
      "type_check": "email",
      "optional": true,
      "stats": {
        "presence_rate": 0.41,
        "multiplicity": 1.0,
        "type_check_pass": 0.998
      }
    },
    "publications": {
      "type": "record_list",
      "container": "//table[contains(@class,'pubs')]//tr[td]",
      "columns": {
        "title": "./td[count(ancestor::table//th[normalize-space()='Title']/preceding-sibling::th)+1]",
        "year": "./td[count(ancestor::table//th[normalize-space()='Year']/preceding-sibling::th)+1]"
      },
      "column_source": "header_row",
      "transforms": {
        "year": [
          "cast(int)"
        ]
      },
      "stats": {
        "presence_rate": 0.77,
        "rows_min": 1,
        "rows_max": 212
      }
    },
    "details": {
      "type": "key_value",
      "pairs": "//dl[@class='profile']/dt",
      "key": ".",
      "value": "./following-sibling::dd[1]",
      "stats": {
        "presence_rate": 0.99,
        "keys_seen": 14
      }
    }
  }
}
```

A page of that template (scripts and `<head>` except `<title>` are stripped before any selector runs):

```html
<html><head><title>Dr. Amal Khoury | Example University</title>
<script>trackPageView();</script></head>
<body>
<header class="site"><nav><a href="/">Home</a> <a href="/staff">Staff</a></nav></header>
<main>
  <header class="profile-head"><h1 itemprop="name">Dr. Amal
      Khoury</h1></header>
  <dl class="profile">
    <dt>Email</dt><dd><a href="mailto:a.khoury@example.org">a.khoury@example.org</a></dd>
    <dt>Office:</dt><dd>Building B, Room 214</dd>
    <dt>Phone</dt><dd>+961 1 350 000 ext. 4321</dd>
  </dl>
  <table class="pubs">
    <tr><th>Year</th><th>Title</th></tr>
    <tr><td>2021</td><td>Wrapper induction with one call per template</td></tr>
    <tr><td>2019</td><td>Template clustering at web scale</td></tr>
  </table>
</main>
</body></html>
```

`Spec.load(path).apply(html)` returns:

```json
{
  "name": "Dr. Amal Khoury",
  "email": "a.khoury@example.org",
  "publications": [
    {
      "title": "Wrapper induction with one call per template",
      "year": 2021
    },
    {
      "title": "Template clustering at web scale",
      "year": 2019
    }
  ],
  "details": {
    "Email": "a.khoury@example.org",
    "Office": "Building B, Room 214",
    "Phone": "+961 1 350 000 ext. 4321"
  },
  "_meta": {
    "missing": [],
    "spec_version": "1"
  }
}
```

`publications` finds its columns by header text even though `Year` comes first on the page; `details` drops the trailing colon of `Office:`.
